title: How To Teach At A Rewards-Focused School
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin acknowledges his well-known opposition to exchanging rewards for expected behavior, but pivots here to offer practical guidance for teachers whose schools mandate token systems like tickets or stickers. Rather than abandon those teachers to a values conflict, he shows how to neutralize the harm by decoupling rewards from specific behaviors entirely: giving them to every student at the same time, for no explained reason, purely as an act of generosity. He outlines three principles — give to everyone, give for fun, and give as a lesson — arguing that unconditional giving models grace and reinforces the idea that learning and belonging are rewards in themselves, rather than turning the classroom into a transactional exchange. Linsin frames this as a way to comply with school mandates while still protecting students from the bribery and manipulation inherent in behavior-contingent rewards, and promises to address related issues like recess tickets in future articles.
points: Teachers required to use token or reward systems can neutralize their harm by decoupling rewards from any specific behavior.
Giving rewards to every student at the same time, for no stated reason, avoids the transactional dynamic of behavior-based rewards.
The three principles are give to everyone, give for fun, and give as a lesson in unconditional generosity.
Unconditional giving models grace and reinforces that learning and belonging are rewards in themselves.
Teachers can stay true to their values around intrinsic motivation even while complying with a school's rewards mandate.
quotes: A do-this-and-get-that approach to classroom management is damaging to kids. It snuffs out intrinsic motivation and turns the student-teacher relationship into a cold-hearted transaction.
The key is to offer them to your students without connecting them to any particular behavior.
If you're required to hand out external rewards, then joyfully give them to everyone in your class at the same time.
Just pass them out at odd times without explanation, even to the student sitting in time-out. It is, after all, a free gift with no strings attached.
Free grace has a remarkable way of softening hearts and reawakening intrinsic motivational engines. It’s also a model for what true giving looks like.
Simple and consistent kindness, pleasantness, and friendliness, without expectation of receiving anything in return, is a core principle here at SCM.
